title: Parkinson-like toxin models: mechanistic plausibility, not human efficacy

Q01.answer: Test neuronal protection and AMPK/autophagy mechanisms. No registered experimental protocol reported. Toxin-induced neuronal injury and cell signaling. Not idiopathic human Parkinson disease.

Q02.answer: Male C57BL/6 mice and human-derived SH-SY5Y cells. Ten-week-old mice; MPTP plus probenecid toxin model. Behavioral/chemistry n=8 per group, histology n=4, MAO-B n=5; three independent cell experiments. No human participants.

Q03.answer: Metformin from Pacific Ocean, Tianjin. Mice: 5 mg/mL drinking water from day three for five weeks; cells: 2 mM pretreatment one hour. MPTP 20 mg/kg plus probenecid 250 mg/kg every 3.5 days; cells MPP+ 200 µM for 48 hours. Mouse motor test day 37; cell assays up to 48 hours. Water concentration is not a measured mg/kg intake or human-equivalent dose.

Q04.answer: Saline, toxin alone, toxin plus metformin and metformin alone. Four mouse groups; cell inhibitor comparisons. Mouse random allocation stated; sequence not described. Stereological assessment blinded; other masking not clearly described. Metformin during toxin exposure, not after longstanding disease. Prevention/co-treatment differs from treating established degeneration.

Q05.answer: Motor, dopamine, neuron counts, inflammatory markers and signaling. Rotarod, HPLC, histology, western blot, PCR and cell viability. Five-week mouse course; short cell exposures. Animal function and mechanistic surrogate outcomes. No validated human clinically meaningful threshold. No human symptom or progression endpoint.

Q06.answer: Toxin rotarod 24.7±8.0 versus toxin-plus-metformin 81.7±11.4, reported as minutes. Eight mice per motor group; four per neuron-count group. Reported 25% higher TH-positive neuron count with metformin versus toxin alone. Dysfunctional mitochondria 19.4% toxin versus 8.5% with metformin, 3.4% untreated cells. Means±SEM and ANOVA/Tukey P values; no clinical effect CI. Do not convert laboratory proportions into patient risk reductions.

Q07.answer: Whole-experiment animal attrition not explicitly tabulated. Missing observations and exclusion criteria not fully documented. Water intake and achieved drug concentration not reported. Different assays use different n. Assay-specific animals or independent culture experiments. Mouse or independent culture; sections/fields are technical observations. Do not count 12 sections per brain as 12 animals.

Q08.answer: No comprehensive toxicology program. Small mouse groups and cell cultures only. Metformin-only controls and viability assays do not measure human adverse effects. Toxicity-related animal withdrawals not reported. Five weeks maximum in mice. Cannot establish safety for older adults.

Q09.answer: Small samples, limited masking detail and pharmacologic inhibitor specificity. Randomized toxin model limits some confounding; no clinical disease heterogeneity. No accessible preregistered analysis plan. Numerous correlated molecular endpoints; Tukey within analyses, not global correction. Small n and no clinically transportable intervals. Rotarod unit reported as minutes; implausibility warrants caution, no silent unit change. Compound C/3MA reversal supports a hypothesis but does not prove a uniquely specific human mechanism.

Q10.answer: Mouse toxin injury and a transformed cell line. Millimolar cell exposure and unmeasured mouse intake do not establish human brain exposure. Indirect rationale only. Does not demonstrate disease modification or symptom benefit in patients. The separate CP016 clinical trial is assessed on its own outcomes.

Q11.answer: This mouse/cell experimental program. Earlier animal work cited; CP016 is separate human evidence. Figures within this paper are not independent clinical replications. Scoped current guide inventory. Multiple assays strengthen triangulation, not clinical certainty.

Q12.answer: Ming Lu, Cunjin Su, Chen Qiao, Yaqi Bian, Jianhua Ding and Gang Hu. Institutional animal and laboratory facilities in China. National Natural Science Foundation of China, national science/technology and Jiangsu grants. Commercial metformin/reagents identified. Statement of Interest: none. Authors’ proposed therapeutic promise remains interpretation.

Q13.answer: Published 2016 experimental report. Full text acquired and methods/results read. No separate supplement relied upon. Not a registered human trial; animal ethics approval reported. No correction/retraction identified in retrieved records. November 3–4, 2026. Targeted appraisal, not forensic image analysis.

Q14.answer: Autophagy and mitochondrial hypotheses. Indirect support for further research only. Observed toxin-model protection; authors speculate about Parkinson therapy; guide makes no human-efficacy inference. No disease-modifying claim.

Q15.answer: Interesting biological rationale with major model/exposure limits. Human target engagement and durable clinical benefit unknown. Adequate randomized human trials with functional outcomes and safety needed. A mechanism is not a treatment result.
